public_rationale: Zitron says Google's generative AI is stapled onto Search and Assistant and users have no choice about it. On March 14, 2025, Google said it was moving mobile Assistant users to Gemini and that classic Assistant would no longer be accessible on most phones later that year. On May 20, 2025, a day before the post, Google said a custom Gemini 2.5 now powers AI Overviews and AI Mode in Search, and that AI features would move into core Search. Reporting from the 2024 rollout found no setting to turn AI Overviews off. 'No choice' overstates things a little. A per-search 'Web' filter hid AI Overviews, and classic Assistant still worked on many phones in May 2025. But the plain reading holds: Google built generative AI into both products by default, with no normal off switch.
limitations: 'No choice' is hyperbole. Workarounds existed, such as the Web filter, URL tricks and other search engines.
The no-off-switch evidence for Search comes from May 2024, not from the target period itself.
The Assistant replacement was announced but not yet complete at the post date.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Google forces generative AI on users by attaching it to Search and Assistant.

statement.excerpt: But don’t worry, Google also has a generative AI thing, for some reason, and no, you don’t have a choice about using it, because it’s now stapled onto Google Search and Google Assistant.
statement.document_title: The Era Of The Business Idiot

from_speaker: Google also has a generative AI thing
you don't have a choice about using it
it's now stapled onto Google Search and Google Assistant
our_interpretation: Plain reading: when the post went out (May 2025), Google had built generative AI into Google Search and Google Assistant by default, without a normal setting that lets users switch it off.

For Search, this means AI Overviews (and the new AI Mode) shown in standard results with no off switch. For Assistant, it means Google moving Assistant users to Gemini and retiring classic Assistant on most phones.

Workarounds such as the 'Web' results filter, URL tricks, or other search engines do not by themselves defeat the plain reading. 'Don't have a choice' is read as 'cannot turn it off in the product', not as 'physically forced to read it'.
The claim describes a current state without naming a period. I use March 1 to May 21, 2025: the period when Google announced the Assistant-to-Gemini switch, up to publication.
criteria.support_condition: Google sources from around the post date show generative AI built into Search results by default and Assistant being replaced by Gemini, and there is no setting to turn AI Overviews off.
criteria.contradiction_condition: As of May 2025, users could simply switch off AI Overviews in Search settings, or Google Assistant was staying as a non-generative assistant with no plan to replace it.

evidence.excerpt: Over the coming months, we’re upgrading more users on mobile devices from Google Assistant to Gemini; and later this year, the classic Google Assistant will no longer be accessible on most mobile devices
evidence.locator: section 'What’s next for Google Assistant', paragraph 2
evidence.explanation: Google said it was replacing Assistant with its generative AI, Gemini, and would make classic Assistant inaccessible on most phones. This supports the claim that generative AI was being attached to Assistant with no lasting opt-out.

evidence.excerpt: As we get feedback, we'll graduate many features and capabilities from AI Mode right into the core Search experience. Starting this week, we're bringing a custom version of Gemini 2.5, our most intelligent model, into Search for both AI Mode and AI Overviews in the U.S.
evidence.locator: section 'AI Mode in Search, for cutting-edge AI capabilities', paragraph 3
evidence.explanation: One day before the post, Google said generative AI (Gemini 2.5) powers AI Overviews in Search and that AI features would move into the core Search experience. This supports 'stapled onto Google Search'.

evidence.excerpt: As of May 20, 2024, there is no built-in option to disable Google AI Overviews within search settings.
evidence.explanation: When AI Overviews rolled out, there was no setting to turn them off. This predates the target period, so it is context for the 'no choice' part, not decisive.

evidence.excerpt: a recently introduced "Web" filter might be a helpful alternative for users who prefer traditional search results.
evidence.explanation: Google offered a per-search 'Web' filter without AI Overviews. This gives users a limited choice and slightly softens 'you don't have a choice', though it is not a setting that turns the feature off.
